meta.title: Ch 12: Ind AS 103 — Business Combinations — MCQ Bank
meta.description: Chapter-wise practice MCQs for Chapter 12 (Ind AS 103 — Business Combinations).

questions.q: Fair value of identifiable net assets acquired (Rs crore):
questions.why: 700 + 300 + 150 + 80 + 20 − 60 = 1,190 crore. Forgetting the assumed obligation (1,250) is the classic miss.
questions.trend: Repeated theme in recent ICAI exam question-patterns for this paper (AI pattern estimate — not a citation to a specific past paper question).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — this topic stays active in ICAI question-setting Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: the assumed-liability adjustment is THE PPA trap FV sweep has two hands: lift the assets, grab the dirty laundry too.

questions.stem: Cobalt Ltd acquires 100% of Dune Ltd for shares worth Rs 1,200 crore. Dune's book net worth is Rs 700 crore. The fair-value sweep identifies: land +300; a registered but unbooked brand +150; a customer list +80; inventory +20 (sells within 9 months); and a pending pollution claim, assessed at Rs 60 crore as probable, absent from Dune's books.

questions.q: Consolidated goodwill (Rs crore):
questions.why: Goodwill = 1,200 − 1,190 = 10. Had the claim been missed the answer would be −50 (bargain purchase) — which itself needs reassessment first.
questions.trend: Fits the style in which ICAI drafts RTP/MTP questions on this topic (pattern estimate; no guarantee of appearance).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — this topic stays active in ICAI question-setting AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: goodwill arithmetic rides on the sweep — one slip flips the story Goodwill is the receipt of the sweep: fix the list, then subtract.

questions.q: The brand (never registered, only internally built) is recognised because:
o: All intangibles in a business are recognised
It is separable and arises from legal rights — identifiable apart from goodwill
It was booked by the seller
questions.why: Ind AS 103 recognises an acquired intangible if identifiable (separable OR from contractual/legal rights); a brand sold/licensed separately qualifies — contrast the prohibition only for INTERNALLY generated brands (Ind AS 38).
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — this topic stays active in ICAI question-setting Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: identifiability-in-combination vs internal prohibition Acquisition unlocks what organic growth bars: the brand is real only when bought.

questions.q: The inventory step-up of Rs 20 crore affects:
o: Consolidated P&L over 9 months as higher cost of sales
questions.why: The written-up inventory sells within 9 months ⇒ the extra 20 flows through COGS in FY26 group P&L (the step-up is a gain that must be 'earned' by selling).
questions.trend: Fits the style in which ICAI drafts RTP/MTP questions on this topic (pattern estimate; no guarantee of appearance).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — this topic stays active in ICAI question-setting AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: amortising the bump is the standard follow-up question Every step-up must walk out the P&L door it came in.

questions.q: Acquisition-related advisory and legal costs of Rs 12 crore are:
questions.why: Ind AS 103 expenses acquisition-cost items when incurred (debt/equity issuance costs follow 109/32).
questions.trend: Repeated theme in recent ICAI exam question-patterns for this paper (AI pattern estimate — not a citation to a specific past paper question).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — this topic stays active in ICAI question-setting Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: the expense-not-capitalise flip keeps testing recall Shopper's costs are shopping's, not the shop's: P&L, day one.

questions.q: In a business combination under Ind AS 103, acquisition-related costs (valuation fees, finder's fees, legal costs) are:
o: Expensed as incurred (except debt/equity issuance costs against the instrument)
questions.why: Transaction costs are expensed when incurred under the acquisition method; costs of issuing debt/equity follow Ind AS 109/32. Contrast the pre-AS-14 regime — this reversal is heavily tested.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — the 'expensed not capitalised' flip is a signature 103 MCQ Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: Business-combination shopping fees: expense at the till. Only share/deal issuance costs ride the instrument.

questions.q: The acquirer previously held a 20% equity interest (equity method) in the acquiree. On obtaining control, the previously-held interest is:
o: Remeasured to fair value at acquisition date with gain/loss in P&L
Remeasured with gain/loss in OCI only
questions.why: Ind AS 103 requires step-acquisition remeasurement of the previously held interest to fair value at the acquisition date; resulting gain/loss to P&L (with recycling of prior OCI where required).
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — step-up gain recognition is a consistent Section B theme AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Second bite bites the balance sheet: old stake → fair value, difference → P&L. Cross that control bridge and you must re-book.

questions.q: In a business combination, contingent consideration payable to sellers is classified as a LIABILITY because it requires delivering a variable cash amount. Post-acquisition changes in that liability's fair value are:
o: Reversal of goodwill with a floor at zero
questions.why: Classification at acquisition decides everything: LIABILITY-classified contingent consideration is remeasured through P&L; equity-classified is NOT remeasured. The old 'goodwill adjustment window' has been removed under Ind AS 103 (2016-aligned amendments).
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the P&L-vs-no-remeasurement split is a trap of the season AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Liability → remeasure to P&L; equity → frozen. Measurement-period adjustments (new info about facts existing at acquisition date, max 12 months) are the only goodwill touchers left.

questions.q: If the acquired set of activities does NOT include a substantive process, the transaction is:
o: An asset acquisition — cost allocated to identifiable assets, no goodwill
questions.why: The screen: outputs exist? If yes, assess substantive process. A set without a substantive process (and without an input-process-output nexus) is not a business ⇒ asset acquisition, no goodwill, transaction costs capitalised.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the screen logic distinguishes pros from guessers Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: No substantive process ⇒ no business ⇒ no goodwill. Screen first, then choose the road.

questions.q: Where the fair value of net identifiable assets acquired exceeds the consideration transferred, the excess is:
o: Recognised in P&L as a gain on bargain purchase AFTER reassessing identification/measurement
questions.why: Reassess → if excess remains, gain to P&L. (Old AS-14 wrote it to capital reserve — the contrast is the trap.)
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the 103-vs-AS-14 contrast is an every-set question Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Bargain purchase: double-check everything, then book the win to P&L. No reserve-hiding anymore.

questions.q: The acquisition date is the date on which the acquirer:
questions.why: Ind AS 103: acquisition date = date the acquirer obtains control (the consideration/contract timing may differ).
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — control-over-contract phrasing Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Signatures propose, control disposes. Measure everything from the day you can direct the relevant activities.

questions.q: Goodwill in a business combination under Ind AS 103 is initially measured as:
o: Consideration + NCI + prior-interest FV − net identifiable assets at FV
questions.why: Goodwill = sum of consideration transferred, NCI and (in step acquisitions) FV of previously held interest, less FV of identifiable net assets — the classic five-term formula.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the formula itself is the 1-marker Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Five-term goodwill: pay + NCI + old stake − assets (all at FV). If the result is negative, retest and call the bargain a gain.

questions.q: Business combinations under common control under ICAI's new-scheme syllabus are covered in the guidance note on common control; the approach generally used is:
o: Pooling of interests (carry-over basis) as per the Guidance Note on Accounting for Amalgamation in Common Control scenarios
questions.why: ICAI's guidance for common-control amalgamations (Guidance Note on Business Combinations under Common Control) permits a pooling-of-interests-type accounting at carry-over book values; ICAI has been aligning with this — the new-scheme syllabus lists BCCC as a study area under Ch 12/AS-14 legacy discussions.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the acquisition-vs-pooling fork for related-entity merges Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Same family merger? Keep the books (pooling); strangers? Re-measure (acquisition).

questions.q: In a reverse acquisition (listed shell acquires operating co), the accounting acquirer is:
o: The entity whose owners control the combined entity (usually the private operating co)
questions.why: Ind AS 103: accounting acquirer = the one obtaining control — in reverse mergers, the legal acquiree's owners dominate ⇒ it 'acquires' the shell; goodwill measured from its perspective.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — substance-of-control questions define advanced 103 papers AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Legal paper flips, but control decides who holds the pen.

questions.q: Part of the 'consideration' paid by the acquirer is actually settlement of a pre-existing lawsuit between them. It is:
o: Excluded from consideration and accounted in P&L as settlement per the acquiror's own situation
questions.why: Pre-existing-relationship settlement amounts are NOT consideration — accounted under other standards (often P&L); identifying them is a classic ICAI trap.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — substance separation of 'consideration' vs settlement AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Some 'purchase price' is really a handshake over a lawsuit — unbundle it before goodwill.

questions.q: Contingent consideration in a business combination is measured at:
questions.why: AC transferred includes the acquisition-date FV of contingent consideration; post-AC changes follow its classification (asset/liability → P&L; equity → not remeasured).
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — AC-at-FV baseline AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Put a price on maybe at the closing table; then let the price live its own life.

questions.q: Pre-acquisition losses of the acquiree affecting deferred tax assets are recognised in AC accounting when:
o: It is probable at AC date that taxable profits will be available (assess in FV of net assets)
questions.why: Acquiree unused tax losses: recognise DTA in PPA if probable at acquisition date; a change in availability after AC → P&L (not goodwill) post-window.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the losses-in-PPA nuance Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Old losses enter goodwill only if they were as good as usable on day one.

questions.q: The measurement period in a business combination:
o: Does not exceed 12 months from the acquisition date
questions.why: Up to 12 months to complete assessments of facts existing at AC date; adjustments restate comparatives (goodwill etc.).
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the 12-month window AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: New facts about old dates have a one-year leash on the books.

questions.q: The new syllabus explicitly lists business combinations under common control (BCCC) within FR. Accounting for BCCC under ICAI's guidance framework generally permits:
o: Carry-over (pooling-type) accounting — book-value continuity, no step-up of all assets to FV, no new goodwill from the reshuffle
questions.why: Structural emphasis: BCCC sit outside the arm's-length acquisition method because ultimate control existed before and after; ICAI guidance (and AS-14 legacy in exam practice) allows book-value continuity — no fresh goodwill, comparatives adjusted per guidance.
questions.trend: Documented syllabus/amendment change — applicability from May 2026 exam onwards per ICAI BoS announcement.
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — newly-explicit syllabus lines get tested to prove they were read AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.ti: TI: New syllabus — BCCC study area
mem.tip: Same family, same books: pool, don't reprice.

questions.q: Cobalt Ltd acquires 75% of an entity for Rs 1100 lakh; FV of identifiable net assets is Rs 1,540 lakh; NCI at proportionate share. After reassessing identification, the acquirer books:
o: Gain of Rs 55 lakh to P&L
questions.why: Consideration 1100 + NCI 385 = 1485 vs net identifiable assets at FV 1540 ⇒ excess 55 lakh recognised in P&L (after reassessment) under Ind AS 103 — capital-reserve treatment belonged to the old AS-14.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the reserve-vs-P&L contrast makes this a reliable 1-marker AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Reassess; if excess persists, P&L gain. Compare FV net assets vs consideration + NCI.
